title: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions (AZ-700) practice questions

exams.name: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: A company plans 20 virtual networks that will later connect to each other and to on premises. What is the most important address planning rule?
options: Use non-overlapping private address ranges across all VNets and on-premises networks
Use 10.0.0.0/16 for every VNet for consistency
Use public IP ranges for private VNets
Use the smallest possible range for each VNet with no room to grow
questions.correct_rationale: Overlapping ranges block peering and routing, so plans must avoid overlap and leave room for growth.
questions.distractor_summary: Reusing one range causes overlap, public ranges cause routing problems, and tiny ranges limit growth.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: How many usable addresses are in a /28 subnet in Azure?
questions.correct_rationale: A /28 has 16 addresses, and Azure reserves five, which leaves 11.
questions.distractor_summary: 16 is the total, 14 ignores Azure's extra reservations, and 8 is wrong.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: Several VMs need contiguous, static public IP addresses that can be allowlisted by partners as one range. What should be used?
options: A public IP address prefix, creating Standard public IPs from it
A NAT gateway without public IPs
questions.correct_rationale: Public IP prefixes reserve a contiguous block of static addresses.
questions.distractor_summary: Dynamic IPs change, private IPs are not public, and NAT gateways need public IPs or prefixes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: Which public IP SKU supports availability zones and is secure by default, closed to inbound traffic unless allowed by an NSG?
questions.correct_rationale: Standard public IPs are zone-aware and closed by default, and Basic IPs have been retired.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is retired, Classic is legacy, and Shared is not a public IP SKU.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: A subnet must be split, but resources already use it. What is the correct approach?
options: Resize the subnet while resources are using addresses outside the new range
Create a new subnet, move resources to it, then delete or resize the old subnet once it is empty
Assign public IPs to all resources
questions.correct_rationale: Subnets in use cannot shrink below the addresses in use, so resources must be moved first.
questions.distractor_summary: Resizing past used addresses fails, VNets cannot change regions, and public IPs do not help.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: Which subnet name is required for Azure Firewall?
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Firewall must be deployed into a subnet named AzureFirewallSubnet.
questions.distractor_summary: GatewaySubnet is for gateways, AzureBastionSubnet is for Bastion, and FirewallSubnet is not a reserved name.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: A VM must keep the same private IP address after reboots and redeployments. What should be configured?
options: Set the NIC's private IP allocation to static
questions.correct_rationale: Static private IP allocation keeps the address assigned to the NIC.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IP settings, extra VNets, and DNS aliases do not fix the private address.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: What is subnet delegation used for?
options: Giving a user admin rights over a subnet
Allowing a specific Azure service to create service-specific resources in a subnet
questions.correct_rationale: Delegation designates a subnet for a service such as Azure SQL Managed Instance or App Service integration.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not user permission, subnet splitting, or IP assignment.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: A VNet must support IPv6 for public-facing workloads. What is required?
options: Replace the IPv4 space with IPv6 only
Add an IPv6 address space and subnet ranges (dual stack), and use Standard SKU IPv6 public IPs and load balancers as needed
questions.correct_rationale: Azure VNets support dual-stack addressing with IPv6 ranges alongside IPv4.
questions.distractor_summary: IPv6-only VNets are not the usual path, Basic is retired, and regions are not needed.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: Which Azure tool helps plan and manage IP address spaces across VNets and subscriptions centrally?
options: Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management (IPAM)
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual Network Manager includes IPAM pools to allocate non-overlapping ranges.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Front Door, and Application Gateway do not plan IP space.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: Outbound connections from many VMs fail with SNAT port exhaustion. What is the best solution?
options: Deploy a NAT gateway with enough public IPs or a public IP prefix on the subnet
questions.correct_rationale: NAT gateway provides many SNAT ports per public IP and scales outbound connections.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs, VM sizes, and DNS do not add SNAT ports.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: VMs in a hub and several spokes must resolve records in contoso.internal. What should be configured?
options: A public DNS zone for contoso.internal
A public IP for each VM
A private DNS zone contoso.internal linked to the hub and spoke VNets
questions.correct_rationale: Linking a private zone to each VNet lets them resolve its records.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones expose names, host files do not scale, and public IPs do not resolve names.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: What does Azure DNS Private Resolver provide?
options: Inbound and outbound endpoints that enable DNS resolution between Azure and on-premises networks without VMs running DNS servers
questions.correct_rationale: Private Resolver forwards queries between environments as a managed service.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not register domains, load balance, or encrypt records.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: On-premises DNS servers must resolve names in Azure private DNS zones. What should be set up?
options: A Private Resolver outbound endpoint only
A Private Resolver inbound endpoint, and conditional forwarders on premises pointing to its IP address
An NSG rule allowing port 53 from the internet
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound endpoints receive queries from on premises and resolve private zones.
questions.distractor_summary: Outbound endpoints send queries from Azure, public zones expose names, and opening port 53 to the internet is risky.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: What is a DNS forwarding ruleset used for in Azure DNS Private Resolver?
options: Defining which domains are forwarded through outbound endpoints to specific DNS servers
questions.correct_rationale: Rulesets map domain names to target DNS servers for forwarding.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not define NSGs, routes, or load balancer rules.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: VMs should register their own DNS records automatically in a private zone. What should be enabled?
options: Auto-registration on the virtual network link
questions.correct_rationale: Auto-registration creates records for VMs in the linked VNet.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones, alias records, and TXT records do not auto-register VMs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: What is the IP address of the Azure-provided DNS resolver reachable from any VNet?
questions.correct_rationale: Azure-provided DNS is reached at 168.63.129.16.
questions.distractor_summary: 8.8.8.8 is a public resolver, 10.0.0.1 is a gateway address, and 169.254.169.254 is the metadata service.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: A private endpoint is created for a storage account, but VMs still resolve the public IP. What is the likely problem?
options: The storage account has soft delete enabled
The VM has too little memory
The privatelink.blob.core.windows.net private DNS zone is missing or not linked to the VNet
questions.correct_rationale: Private endpoints rely on private DNS zones to resolve the service name to the private IP.
questions.distractor_summary: Soft delete, VM memory, and NSG rules do not affect name resolution.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: Which record type in Azure DNS can point directly to an Azure resource such as a public IP, updating automatically if the IP changes?
options: A CNAME to a hard-coded IP
questions.correct_rationale: Alias records reference Azure resources and track their changes.
questions.distractor_summary: CNAMEs point to names, MX is for mail, and SRV is for services.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: A public domain must be hosted in Azure. What should be done after creating the public DNS zone?
options: Link the zone to a VNet
Delegate the domain by setting the zone's Azure name servers at the registrar
questions.correct_rationale: Delegation points the domain to Azure DNS name servers.
questions.distractor_summary: VNet links apply to private zones, inbound endpoints are for private resolution, and NSGs are unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement name resolution
questions.question: Which feature lets one private DNS zone be resolved from many VNets in a hub-and-spoke design with on-premises forwarding through a central point?
options: A separate copy of each zone in each spoke with no links
Centralized private DNS zones linked to the hub, with a Private Resolver in the hub and spokes using it as their DNS server
Public DNS zones for internal records
questions.correct_rationale: Central zones and a resolver in the hub simplify private DNS across spokes.
questions.distractor_summary: Copies drift, public zones expose names, and host files do not scale.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Spoke VNets must send all internet-bound traffic through a firewall in the hub. What should be configured in each spoke?
options: A route table with 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the firewall's private IP as a virtual appliance next hop
A NAT gateway in each spoke
VNet peering with gateway transit disabled only
A public IP on every VM
questions.correct_rationale: User-defined routes force traffic to the firewall.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways bypass the firewall, peering settings alone do not route traffic, and public IPs bypass it.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: What is the effect of the Use remote gateways setting on a spoke peering?
options: The spoke gets its own gateway
Traffic is blocked to the hub
The spoke uses the hub's VPN or ExpressRoute gateway to reach on premises
questions.correct_rationale: Use remote gateways, paired with Allow gateway transit in the hub, shares the hub's gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: The spoke does not get its own gateway, traffic is not blocked, and roles do not swap.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: A network virtual appliance must learn routes dynamically from Azure VNets and advertise on-premises routes without static UDRs. Which service fits?
options: Azure Route Server, peering with the NVA over BGP
questions.correct_rationale: Route Server exchanges routes between NVAs and the VNet using BGP.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Application Gateway, and Front Door do not exchange routes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Which next-hop type in a user-defined route drops traffic?
questions.correct_rationale: A route with next hop None drops matching traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: The other types forward traffic.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: A subnet route table should not receive on-premises routes learned by the VPN gateway. What setting should be changed?
options: Disable gateway route propagation on the route table
questions.correct_rationale: Disabling propagation stops BGP routes from the gateway being added to that subnet.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the gateway breaks connectivity, and NSGs or prefixes do not affect routes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: What is Azure Virtual Network Manager used for?
options: Centrally managing connectivity, such as hub-and-spoke or mesh topologies, and security admin rules across VNets and subscriptions
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual Network Manager groups VNets and applies connectivity and security configurations at scale.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not host sites, store DNS, or back up VMs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Spokes must communicate directly with each other in a hub-and-spoke topology without traffic going through the hub. What can Virtual Network Manager configure?
options: A NAT gateway in every spoke
A private DNS zone per spoke
A hub-and-spoke connectivity configuration with direct connectivity enabled between spokes in a network group
questions.correct_rationale: Direct connectivity creates connected groups so spokes reach each other directly.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways, DNS zones, and load balancers do not create spoke connectivity.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Which statement about global VNet peering is correct?
options: It sends traffic over the public internet
It is limited to the same subscription
It connects VNets in different regions over the Microsoft backbone with private IPs
questions.correct_rationale: Global peering connects regions privately and works across subscriptions and tenants.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not use the internet, does not need gateways, and is not limited to one subscription.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: A VNet in one tenant must be peered with a VNet in another tenant. What is required?
options: Moving both VNets to one tenant first
A VPN gateway in each VNet
Users with permissions in both VNets create the peering from each side, for example using a user that has access in both tenants
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-tenant peering is supported when the right permissions exist on both sides.
questions.distractor_summary: Moving tenants is unnecessary, gateways are not required, and public IPs do not create peering.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Which route source wins when a BGP route and a system route have the same prefix?
questions.correct_rationale: The order is user-defined, then BGP, then system routes for identical prefixes.
questions.distractor_summary: System routes lose to BGP, creation time does not matter, and traffic is not dropped.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: Asymmetric routing breaks connections through two NVAs behind a load balancer. What design fixes it?
options: Use an internal Standard load balancer with HA ports for both inbound and return traffic so flows stay on the same NVA
Remove the load balancer and use DNS round robin
Use public IPs on the NVAs
questions.correct_rationale: HA ports with the same load balancer keep flow symmetry through the same appliance.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS round robin does not guarantee symmetry, public IPs bypass design, and Basic is retired.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement VNet connectivity and routing
questions.question: What is service chaining in Azure networking?
options: Directing traffic through a network virtual appliance using user-defined routes across peered VNets
questions.correct_rationale: Service chaining uses UDRs to send peered traffic through an appliance.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not link DNS zones, storage accounts, or App Service plans.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: A team must continuously monitor connectivity and latency from Azure VMs to an on-premises server. What should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: Connection monitor runs ongoing tests and alerts on loss and latency.
questions.distractor_summary: IP flow verify checks rules once, Advisor recommends, and NSGs filter.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Which Network Watcher tool checks whether a packet is allowed or denied by NSG rules for a VM?
questions.correct_rationale: IP flow verify reports the rule that allows or denies a specific flow.
questions.distractor_summary: Packet capture records traffic, topology maps resources, and VPN troubleshoot diagnoses gateways.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Traffic patterns across VNets must be analyzed to find top talkers and malicious flows. What should be configured?
options: Virtual network flow logs with traffic analytics in a Log Analytics workspace
questions.correct_rationale: Traffic analytics processes flow logs to show patterns, top talkers, and threats.
questions.distractor_summary: Activity logs show control plane events, Advisor recommends, and Application Insights monitors apps.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: What does the Network Watcher topology feature show?
options: A list of costs by resource
A visual map of resources in a VNet and how they connect
questions.correct_rationale: Topology shows network resources and their relationships.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not show costs, traces, or sign-ins.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: A site-to-site VPN connection is down. Which Network Watcher tool diagnoses gateway and connection problems?
questions.correct_rationale: VPN troubleshoot checks gateway health and connection status and gives logs.
questions.distractor_summary: Next hop, IP flow verify, and effective routes focus on other areas.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Which metric indicates the bandwidth used by a VPN gateway?
options: Gateway S2S bandwidth or tunnel bandwidth metrics in Azure Monitor
questions.correct_rationale: VPN gateway metrics show tunnel and gateway bandwidth.
questions.distractor_summary: VM CPU, storage, and DNS metrics do not show gateway bandwidth.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: A VM cannot reach a destination, and the team suspects routing. Which tool shows all routes applied to the VM's NIC?
options: Effective routes on the network interface
questions.correct_rationale: Effective routes show system, BGP, and user-defined routes in effect.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor, Resource health, and cost analysis do not show routes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Which service gives a central view of network health metrics and topology for many Azure network resources?
questions.correct_rationale: Network Insights shows health and metrics for network resources across subscriptions.
questions.distractor_summary: Boards, Artifacts, and Purview are unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Flow logs consume too much storage. How can costs be reduced while keeping useful data?
options: Set a retention period on flow log storage, use lifecycle policies, and enable traffic analytics with a longer processing interval if suitable
questions.correct_rationale: Retention, lifecycle rules, and processing intervals control cost.
questions.distractor_summary: Turning logs off loses data, duplication adds cost, and weekend logging leaves gaps.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Which tool records network packets on a VM for a set time and saves them for analysis?
questions.correct_rationale: Packet capture records traffic to storage or local files.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools analyze configuration or test connectivity.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: An ExpressRoute circuit must be monitored for BGP availability and packet drops. Where can this be seen?
options: ExpressRoute metrics and Network Insights in Azure Monitor, with alerts
questions.correct_rationale: ExpressRoute publishes BGP and ARP availability and traffic metrics.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost recommendations, app logs, and Storage Explorer do not show circuit health.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: What does the Network Watcher next hop tool show?
options: The cost of the next resource
The next hop type and IP address for traffic from a VM to a destination, and which route applies
questions.correct_rationale: Next hop helps diagnose routing issues.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not show cost, maintenance, or DNS servers.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Network Watcher tools are not available in a region. What is the likely reason?
options: Network Watcher is not enabled in that region, so it must be enabled (it is usually created automatically in the NetworkWatcherRG resource group)
The VNet has a private DNS zone
questions.correct_rationale: Network Watcher is regional and must exist in the region.
questions.distractor_summary: Budgets, disks, and DNS zones do not affect availability.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Monitor networks
questions.question: Which feature shows the security rules that combine from all NSGs for a NIC?
questions.correct_rationale: Effective security rules show the combined NSG rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Effective routes show routes, and the others test connectivity or VPNs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: Which type of VPN gateway supports multiple site-to-site connections, point-to-site, and coexistence with ExpressRoute?
questions.correct_rationale: Route-based gateways support these scenarios, while policy-based gateways are limited.
questions.distractor_summary: Policy-based gateways are limited, Basic SKU lacks features, and route-based gateways do support them.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: A site-to-site VPN must survive the failure of one gateway instance. What should be configured?
options: An active-active VPN gateway with tunnels from on-premises devices to both instances
A single active-standby gateway with one tunnel
questions.correct_rationale: Active-active gateways keep both instances active for faster failover.
questions.distractor_summary: One tunnel has more downtime, and VNets or NAT gateways do not add VPN resilience.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: What does a local network gateway represent in Azure?
options: The on-premises VPN device's public IP and address prefixes or BGP settings
questions.correct_rationale: The local network gateway describes the remote site.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not the Azure gateway, a load balancer, or DNS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: A site-to-site VPN must use specific IPsec encryption algorithms required by security policy. What should be configured?
options: A custom IPsec/IKE policy on the connection
questions.correct_rationale: Custom IPsec/IKE policies set algorithms, DH groups, and lifetimes.
questions.distractor_summary: SKU size does not set algorithms, NSGs on GatewaySubnet are not supported, and DNS is unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: On-premises sites and Azure must exchange routes dynamically, and failover between tunnels must be automatic. What should be enabled?
options: BGP on the VPN gateway and the local network gateways
questions.correct_rationale: BGP exchanges routes and supports automatic failover.
questions.distractor_summary: Static routes need manual updates, NAT gateways handle outbound, and policy-based routing is limited.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: Which gateway SKUs support zone redundancy for VPN gateways?
options: SKUs ending in AZ, such as VpnGw2AZ
questions.correct_rationale: AZ SKUs deploy gateway instances across availability zones.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is not zone-redundant, load balancer SKUs are unrelated, and non-AZ SKUs are not zone-redundant.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: On-premises and Azure address spaces overlap, and a site-to-site VPN must still work for specific hosts. What can help?
options: NAT rules on the VPN gateway to translate overlapping prefixes
questions.correct_rationale: VPN gateway NAT can map overlapping address spaces.
questions.distractor_summary: BGP, DNS, and policy-based gateways do not translate addresses.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: Which statement about the GatewaySubnet is correct?
options: It needs a public IP on each address
It must be named GatewaySubnet, should be /27 or larger, and should not have NSGs or other resources
questions.correct_rationale: GatewaySubnet is reserved for gateway instances and needs enough space.
questions.distractor_summary: VMs should not be placed there, /32 is too small, and addresses do not need public IPs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a site-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: Two Azure VNets in different regions must be connected through VPN gateways with encryption. What connection type should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: VNet-to-VNet connects VNets through VPN gateways over IPsec.
questions.distractor_summary: P2S is for clients, Microsoft peering is for public services, and service endpoints serve PaaS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services

Forcing VMs to use public IPs
Sending internet-bound traffic from Azure back to on premises for inspection

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services

questions.distractor_summary: SSTP certificate auth does not use Entra, IKEv2 does not support Entra auth, and S2S is for sites.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: Which authentication methods are supported for P2S VPN in Azure?
options: Certificate, Microsoft Entra ID, and RADIUS

questions.distractor_summary: Shared passwords, SSH keys, and no authentication are not supported options.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: A user's P2S client certificate is compromised. What should be done?
options: Add the certificate's thumbprint to the revoked certificates list on the gateway
questions.correct_rationale: Revoking the client certificate blocks that client.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the gateway affects everyone, and storage keys or address spaces are unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: What is the client address pool in a P2S configuration?
options: A list of allowed public IPs
A private IP range assigned to connecting clients, which must not overlap the VNet or on-premises ranges
questions.correct_rationale: Clients get addresses from the pool when they connect.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not an allowlist, the VNet range, or DNS servers.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: P2S users must reach on-premises networks connected through the same VPN gateway. What must be ensured?

The P2S client routes include the on-premises prefixes, for example by BGP or by downloading the updated client profile
The users disable the VPN client
questions.correct_rationale: Clients need routes for on-premises prefixes, delivered through the profile or configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs, NAT gateways, and disabling the client do not provide routes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection

questions.correct_rationale: SSTP and OpenVPN can use TLS over TCP 443, which passes most firewalls.
questions.distractor_summary: GRE and L2TP are blocked more often, and SMB is file sharing.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage a point-to-site VPN connection
questions.question: After changing VNet peering or address space, P2S users cannot reach new subnets. What should be done?
options: Download and reinstall the updated VPN client configuration
Change the client address pool to overlap the VNet
questions.correct_rationale: Client profiles contain routes and must be refreshed after topology changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the gateway is disruptive, overlap breaks routing, and route propagation is unrelated to client routes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services

questions.question: Which ExpressRoute peering type is used to connect to VNets?
questions.correct_rationale: Private peering connects on-premises networks to VNets.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute

options: Access to Microsoft public services such as Microsoft 365 and Azure PaaS public endpoints over ExpressRoute

questions.distractor_summary: Private peering reaches VNets, it is not general internet access, and it is not DNS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services

ExpressRoute Global Reach between the circuits

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: Which feature sends traffic from on premises directly to VMs, bypassing the ExpressRoute gateway in the data path for better performance?
questions.correct_rationale: FastPath improves data path performance by bypassing the gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: Global Reach links circuits, route filters select prefixes, and BFD detects failures.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services

options: A standard provider circuit at 50 Mbps
questions.correct_rationale: ExpressRoute Direct provides dual 10 or 100 Gbps ports.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: What is required before routes are advertised over Microsoft peering?

questions.distractor_summary: NSGs, DNS zones, and Global Reach are not required.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: An ExpressRoute circuit is the primary path, and a VPN is the backup. How should coexistence be designed?

Deploy both an ExpressRoute gateway and a route-based VPN gateway in the GatewaySubnet, with BGP so ExpressRoute is preferred

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: Which ExpressRoute SKU allows connecting to VNets in any region worldwide from a circuit?
questions.correct_rationale: Premium extends connectivity to all regions globally, while Standard covers a geopolitical region.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: A company wants ExpressRoute with no egress data transfer charges and connects to regions near its peering location. Which SKU fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Local circuits include data transfer and reach regions close to the peering location.
questions.distractor_summary: Premium and Standard metered charge for data differently, and VPN is a different service.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: What does ExpressRoute circuit resiliency depend on?
options: Using both primary and secondary connections, and ideally circuits in different peering locations
questions.correct_rationale: Redundant connections and locations protect against failures.
questions.distractor_summary: One connection is a single point of failure, disabling BGP breaks routing, and public IPs are unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Design, implement, and manage Azure ExpressRoute
questions.question: Encryption is required over ExpressRoute private peering. What options exist?
options: Run IPsec VPN over ExpressRoute private peering, or use MACsec on ExpressRoute Direct
ExpressRoute encrypts all traffic by default
questions.correct_rationale: ExpressRoute does not encrypt by default, so IPsec or MACsec adds encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: Default encryption is not provided, NSGs do not encrypt, and Microsoft peering does not encrypt.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: What is Azure Virtual WAN?
options: A networking service that brings VPN, ExpressRoute, and VNet connectivity together in Microsoft-managed hubs
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual WAN provides managed hubs with transit connectivity.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not DNS, a WAF, or a backup service.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: A company needs any-to-any transit between branches, VNets, and users through managed hubs. Which Virtual WAN type is required?
questions.correct_rationale: Standard Virtual WAN supports full transit and ExpressRoute, while Basic supports only S2S VPN.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is limited, and Premium and Local are not Virtual WAN types.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: What is a virtual hub in Azure Virtual WAN?
options: A Microsoft-managed virtual network that hosts gateways and connects VNets and branches
questions.correct_rationale: Hubs contain gateways and routing for Virtual WAN.
questions.distractor_summary: Hubs are not laptops, storage, or DNS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: Traffic between VNets connected to a Virtual WAN hub must be inspected by Azure Firewall. What should be configured?
options: A secured virtual hub with Azure Firewall and routing intent for private traffic
A NAT gateway in each spoke
questions.correct_rationale: Routing intent sends private traffic through the hub firewall.
questions.distractor_summary: Hubs do not use NSGs for this, spoke peering bypasses the hub, and NAT gateways handle outbound.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: Which component lets you control routing between VNet connections and branches in a Virtual WAN hub?
options: Hub route tables with associations and propagations
questions.correct_rationale: Route tables define how connections route through the hub.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs, DNS zones, and listeners do not control hub routing.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: Branch offices with SD-WAN devices must connect automatically to Virtual WAN. What helps?
options: Using partner devices that integrate with Virtual WAN to automate branch connections
Manually creating VNets for each branch
questions.correct_rationale: Partner integration automates device and tunnel configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: VNets per branch, P2S, and load balancers do not automate SD-WAN.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: A global company has branches in several continents and wants traffic to use the Microsoft backbone between them. What design fits?
options: A single hub with VPNs from every continent
Virtual WAN hubs in several regions, which connect to each other automatically with hub-to-hub transit
questions.correct_rationale: Multiple hubs in a Standard Virtual WAN are connected in a full mesh.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: Which statement about Virtual WAN point-to-site VPN is correct?
options: P2S is not supported in Virtual WAN
User VPN gateways in hubs let remote users connect and reach VNets and branches
P2S users must have static IPs
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual WAN supports User VPN in hubs.
questions.distractor_summary: P2S is supported, needs no ExpressRoute, and users need no static IPs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: A Network virtual appliance must be deployed inside the Virtual WAN hub. Is this possible?
options: No, hubs only support Azure Firewall
Yes, certain partner NVAs can be deployed into the hub
Yes, but only with a Basic Virtual WAN
Yes, any VM can be deployed in a hub
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual WAN supports partner NVAs in the hub, along with Azure Firewall.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: What does routing intent do in Virtual WAN?
options: It assigns public IPs to VMs
It defines that internet or private traffic should go through a security solution in the hub, such as Azure Firewall
questions.correct_rationale: Routing intent simplifies sending traffic through hub security.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not assign IPs, create DNS records, or define load balancer rules.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.subdomain: Connect networks by using Azure Virtual WAN
questions.question: A VNet connected to a Virtual WAN hub must not reach another VNet connected to the same hub. How can this be done?
options: Associate and propagate the VNet connections to separate custom route tables so they do not learn each other's routes
questions.correct_rationale: Custom route tables isolate connections in Virtual WAN.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the hub breaks everything, and NAT gateways and DNS do not isolate routing.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: What happens to a Standard SKU public IP address when the VM it is attached to is stopped and deallocated?
options: The address moves to another subscription
The address is kept, because Standard public IPs use static allocation
questions.correct_rationale: Static Standard IPs stay with the resource until deleted or disassociated.
questions.distractor_summary: Static addresses are not released, do not change version, and do not move subscriptions.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.subdomain: Design and implement IP addressing for Azure resources
questions.question: An application needs outbound traffic to come from a fixed set of public IPs, and no inbound access. What is the best option?

A public load balancer with inbound rules
A NAT gateway with a public IP prefix
questions.correct_rationale: NAT gateway gives predictable outbound IPs without inbound exposure.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure

That the private endpoints have public IPs
That the new spoke's DNS server setting points to the inbound endpoint and that the spoke is peered to the hub
That the spoke's NSG allows port 3389

questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure

questions.domain: 1. Design and implement core networking infrastructure

An activity log alert for write and delete operations on network security groups

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions

questions.question: A public web app needs protection from SQL injection and cross-site scripting at a regional layer 7 entry point. What should be used?
options: Application Gateway WAF_v2 with a managed rule set
questions.correct_rationale: WAF managed rules protect against OWASP threats.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs work at layer 4, NAT gateways handle outbound, and Traffic Manager is DNS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: What is the difference between WAF Detection and Prevention modes?
options: Detection blocks requests, while Prevention only logs
Detection logs threats without blocking, while Prevention blocks matching requests
questions.correct_rationale: Detection is for tuning, and Prevention enforces.
questions.distractor_summary: The modes are reversed or merged in the other choices.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: A WAF managed rule blocks legitimate requests that contain a specific form field. What should be done?
options: Add an exclusion for that field on the relevant rule, or tune the rule, after checking logs
Switch the whole policy to Detection permanently
questions.correct_rationale: Exclusions narrow rule scope while keeping protection.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling or permanent Detection removes protection, and deleting the app is absurd.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: Which WAF custom rule type limits requests from a client over a time window?
options: A match rule on headers only
questions.correct_rationale: Rate limit rules throttle clients that exceed thresholds.
questions.distractor_summary: Match rules filter by conditions, managed rule sets are predefined, and exclusions skip inspection.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: Traffic from certain countries must be blocked at the edge for a global app. What should be configured?
options: A custom geo-match rule in the Front Door WAF policy
questions.correct_rationale: Front Door WAF supports geo-filtering at the edge.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs work at regional subnets, and DNS and NAT gateways do not filter by country.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: Which WAF feature on Front Door Premium protects against automated threats such as scrapers?
options: The bot protection (bot manager) rule set
questions.correct_rationale: Bot manager rules classify and act on bot traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Draining, probes, and affinity are not WAF features.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Load Balancer and Azure Traffic Manager
questions.question: A Traffic Manager profile must distribute 80 percent of traffic to one endpoint and 20 percent to another for a gradual migration. Which routing method fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Weighted routing splits traffic by assigned weights.
questions.distractor_summary: Priority uses one endpoint, performance picks lowest latency, and subnet routes by client IP range.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Load Balancer and Azure Traffic Manager
questions.question: What is a nested Traffic Manager profile?
options: A profile used as an endpoint in another profile, combining routing methods
A profile stored in a private DNS zone
A load balancer inside a VNet
A profile limited to one region
questions.correct_rationale: Nesting lets you combine methods, such as performance across regions and weighted within a region.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not stored in private DNS, is not a load balancer, and is not region-limited.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Load Balancer and Azure Traffic Manager
questions.question: Clients connected to a load balancer have idle connections dropped after a few minutes. What setting helps?
options: Increase the idle timeout on the load balancing rule and enable TCP reset, or use application keep-alives
questions.correct_rationale: Idle timeout and TCP reset settings control how idle flows are handled.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is retired, removing probes breaks health checks, and DNS is unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Application Gateway
questions.question: Application Gateway must check backend health using a specific host header and path. What should be configured?
options: The default probe with no changes
A custom health probe with the host name and path
questions.correct_rationale: Custom probes let you set host, path, interval, and matching status codes.
questions.distractor_summary: The default probe may not use the right host or path, and NSGs and Traffic Manager do not probe backends.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Application Gateway
questions.question: Which Application Gateway v2 capability allows it to scale automatically between a minimum and maximum instance count?
questions.correct_rationale: v2 supports autoscaling within configured limits.
questions.distractor_summary: Draining, rewrites, and affinity are unrelated to scaling.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Front Door
questions.question: Content cached in Front Door is out of date after a deployment. What should be done?
options: Purge the cache for the affected paths or the whole endpoint
questions.correct_rationale: Purging removes cached content so new content is fetched.
questions.distractor_summary: Restarts, deletion, and DNS changes do not clear edge caches.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement application delivery services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Front Door
questions.question: Which Front Door setting controls whether query strings are part of the cache key?
options: Query string caching behavior on the route or rule set
questions.correct_rationale: Caching settings decide whether query strings vary cached content.
questions.distractor_summary: Priority, probes, and domain validation do not change cache keys.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Private Link service and Azure private endpoints
questions.question: An App Service web app must be reached only privately from a VNet. What should be configured?
options: A private endpoint for the web app, with the privatelink.azurewebsites.net DNS zone and public access disabled
questions.correct_rationale: Private endpoints provide private inbound access to App Service.
questions.distractor_summary: Service endpoints restrict sources but keep public access, VNet integration handles outbound calls, and NAT gateways are outbound.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Private Link service and Azure private endpoints
questions.question: Which sub-resource (group ID) is chosen when creating a private endpoint for Azure Files?
questions.correct_rationale: Each storage service has its own sub-resource, and Azure Files uses file.
questions.distractor_summary: blob, queue, and sqlServer are for other services.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Private Link service and Azure private endpoints
questions.question: A storage account needs private endpoints for both blob and file services. How many private endpoints are needed?
options: One private endpoint covers all storage services
Zero, because service endpoints are enough
questions.correct_rationale: Private endpoints are created per sub-resource.
questions.distractor_summary: One endpoint does not cover all services, service endpoints differ, and containers do not need separate endpoints.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Private Link service and Azure private endpoints
questions.question: Which tool shows whether DNS for a private endpoint resolves correctly from a VM?
options: Running nslookup or Resolve-DnsName for the service FQDN from the VM
questions.correct_rationale: Name resolution tests show whether the private IP is returned.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor, cost analysis, and Application Insights do not test DNS.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement service endpoints
questions.question: Which Azure services commonly support service endpoints?
options: Azure Storage, Azure SQL Database, Azure Key Vault, and Azure Cosmos DB, among others
questions.correct_rationale: Many PaaS services support service endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: VMs, DNS, and Application Gateway are not service endpoint targets.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement service endpoints
questions.question: After a service endpoint is enabled, what source IP does the Azure service see from VMs in the subnet?
questions.correct_rationale: With service endpoints, traffic uses private source IPs on the backbone.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not use public, random, or NAT gateway IPs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement service endpoints
questions.question: A subnet with a service endpoint for Storage must still reach storage accounts in other regions. What applies?
options: Service endpoints cover every region worldwide
Service endpoints block all other regions
Service endpoints need ExpressRoute for other regions
Storage service endpoints cover accounts in the same region and the paired region, so others are reached over the public endpoint unless private endpoints are used
questions.correct_rationale: Service endpoint coverage for Storage is limited by region.
questions.distractor_summary: Coverage is not global, does not block other regions, and does not need ExpressRoute.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Implement and manage network security groups
questions.question: An NSG rule must allow traffic to a group of Azure SQL addresses in one region without listing IPs. What should be used?
options: A list of IPs copied from a website
The Sql.<region> service tag as the destination
questions.correct_rationale: Regional service tags represent service IP ranges.
questions.distractor_summary: IP lists go stale, ASGs group your NICs, and DNS does not filter traffic.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Implement and manage network security groups
questions.question: Which NSG default rule denies all inbound traffic not matched by another rule?
questions.correct_rationale: DenyAllInBound has priority 65500 and denies anything not allowed earlier.
questions.distractor_summary: The others allow specific traffic.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Implement and manage network security groups
questions.question: Can an NSG rule reference application security groups that contain NICs from different VNets?
options: No, all NICs in an ASG must be in the same VNet, and the rule's ASGs must belong to the same VNet
Yes, but only with public IPs
questions.correct_rationale: ASG members must be in the same VNet.
questions.distractor_summary: ASGs do not span VNets, and regions or public IPs do not change this.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager
questions.question: Azure Firewall must be highly available across zones in a region. What should be configured?
options: Deploy the firewall with availability zones selected
Deploy two firewalls in different subscriptions with no routing
Use a Basic load balancer in front of the firewall
questions.correct_rationale: Zone-redundant deployment protects against zone failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Unrelated firewalls, Basic load balancers, and one zone do not provide zone redundancy.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager
questions.question: What is an IP group in Azure Firewall?
options: A reusable collection of IP addresses and ranges used in firewall rules
questions.correct_rationale: IP groups simplify rule management.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not user groups, pools, or zones.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager
questions.question: A spoke-to-spoke flow through Azure Firewall works one way but fails the other. What is a likely cause?
options: Missing or asymmetric UDRs in one spoke, so return traffic bypasses the firewall
questions.correct_rationale: Both spokes need routes through the firewall for symmetric flows.
questions.distractor_summary: Rule counts, SKU, and DNS proxy do not cause one-way failures.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager
questions.question: Which Azure Firewall rule collection type is evaluated for traffic based on IP, port, and protocol?
options: DNAT rule collection only for outbound
questions.correct_rationale: Network rules filter by layer 3 and 4 attributes.
questions.distractor_summary: Application rules use FQDNs, DNAT handles inbound translation, and web categories are application-level.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager
questions.question: Firewall policies must be deployed to secured virtual hubs and hub VNets from one place. Which service manages this?
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager centrally manages policies across hubs and VNets.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Application Gateway, and Traffic Manager do not manage firewall policies.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: A WAF policy must be shared by several Application Gateway listeners with different rules for one site. What can be done?
options: Use one policy for all sites with no exceptions
Associate a global WAF policy with the gateway and a per-site WAF policy with a specific listener
questions.correct_rationale: WAF policies can be assigned at gateway, listener, or path level.
questions.distractor_summary: One policy may not fit all sites, disabling removes protection, and NSGs are not WAFs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: Which managed rule set is used by Azure WAF on Application Gateway for core OWASP protections?
options: The OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS) or the Microsoft Default Rule Set (DRS)
The Azure Policy guest configuration set
questions.correct_rationale: Application Gateway WAF uses CRS or DRS managed rule sets.
questions.distractor_summary: Policy, NSG, and DNS rules are not WAF rule sets.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: WAF logs must be analyzed to find which rules block the most requests. What should be configured?
options: Diagnostic settings sending WAF logs to Log Analytics, then KQL queries grouped by rule ID
questions.correct_rationale: WAF diagnostic logs include rule IDs and actions for analysis.
questions.distractor_summary: The activity log lacks request details, and Storage Explorer and Advisor do not analyze WAF logs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions
questions.domain: 5. Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployment
questions.question: Where can a WAF policy be attached to protect a global web application at the edge?
questions.correct_rationale: Front Door WAF policies inspect requests at Microsoft's edge locations.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs, NAT gateways, and DNS zones cannot host WAF policies.
